citations.locator: 26 C.F.R. § 1.6043-1(a) ('Within 30 days after the adoption of any resolution or plan for or in respect of the dissolution of a corporation or the liquidation of the whole or any part of its capital stock', the corporation 'shall file a return on Form 966, containing the information required by paragraph (b) of this section and by such form'), § 1.6043-1(b) (contents of the return)

C. § 281(b) ('A dissolved corporation or successor entity which has not followed the procedures described in § 280 of this title shall, prior to the expiration of the period described in § 278 of this title, adopt a plan of distribution' that pays or makes reasonable provision for known claims and obligations including contingent and unmatured contractual claims, for compensation in pending actions, and for claims likely to arise or become known within 10 years after dissolution, with remaining assets then distributable to stockholders)

citations.title: Companies Act 2006, section 1003: Striking off on application by company
citations.locator: Companies Act 2006 s 1003(1) ('On application by a company, the registrar of companies may strike the company's name off the register.'), s 1003(2) (the application must be made on the company's behalf by its directors or by a majority of them and contain the prescribed information), s 1003(3) (the registrar may not strike the company off until 2 months after publishing a Gazette notice that states the power may be exercised and invites objections)
citations.note: Revised official text fetched live 2026-10-21 ('Latest available (Revised)'). Check the live text before relying.

citations.title: Companies Act 2006, section 1004: Circumstances in which application not to be made: activities of company
citations.locator: Companies Act 2006 s 1004(1) (the s 1003 application must not be made if at any time in the previous 3 months the company has changed its name, traded or otherwise carried on business, disposed for value of property it held for disposal for gain in the normal course of trading, or engaged in any other activity except one necessary for making the application, concluding the company's affairs, meeting a statutory requirement, or an activity specified by the Secretary of State), s 1004(5)-(7) (contravention is an offence, with a defence of showing the person did not know and could not reasonably have known of the facts leading to the contravention)

Check the live text before relying.

citations.title: Insolvency Act 1986, section 89: Statutory declaration of solvency
citations.locator: Insolvency Act 1986 s 89(1) (the directors may make a statutory declaration that they have made a full inquiry into the company's affairs and have formed the opinion that the company will be able to pay its debts in full, together with interest at the official rate, within a period not exceeding 12 months from the commencement of the winding up), s 89(2) (the declaration has no effect unless made within the 5 weeks immediately preceding the date the winding-up resolution passes, or on that date but before the resolution, and it embodies a statement of the company's assets and liabilities as at the latest practicable date)
citations.note: Revised official text fetched live 2026-10-21, incorporating Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 amendments. Check the live text before relying.

citations.title: Insolvency Act 1986, section 90: Distinction between 'members'' and 'creditors'' voluntary winding up
citations.locator: Insolvency Act 1986 s 90 ('A winding up in the case of which a directors' statutory declaration under section 89 has been made is a "members' voluntary winding up"; and a winding up in the case of which such a declaration has not been made is a "creditors' voluntary winding up".')
citations.note: Revised official text fetched live 2026-10-21. Section 100 (the liquidator in a creditors' voluntary winding up is the person nominated by the creditors or, where none, the company's nominee) verified live the same day. Check the live text before relying.

citations.publisher: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
citations.title: Article 9-A — Franchise tax on general business corporations
citations.locator: 'Corporations must file and pay the franchise tax on general business corporations if they are: a domestic corporation (incorporated in New York State); or a foreign corporation (incorporated outside New York State) that does business, employs capital, owns or leases property, maintains an office, or derives receipts from activity, in New York State'; the return is Form CT-3 (CT-3-A for combined filers); tax is the highest of business income, business capital, and fixed dollar minimum bases plus any MTA surcharge
citations.note: Agency guidance fetched live 2026-10-22; the page states it covers tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 and before January 1, 2026 — recheck for later years.

citations.publisher: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
citations.title: Deriving receipts for Article 9-A tax and MTA surcharge
citations.locator: Deriving-receipts thresholds: '$1,000,000 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2015, and before January 1, 2022; $1,138,000 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2022, and before January 1, 2024; and $1,283,000 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, and before January 1, 2027'; the Commissioner reviews the thresholds annually against CPI (20 NYCRR 1-2.8, 8-1.1)
citations.note: Agency guidance fetched live 2026-10-22. Thresholds are indexed — recheck for tax years beginning 2027 or later.

citations.title: Deadline & requirements for annual returns
citations.locator: 'All companies registered in Singapore must file an annual return with ACRA each year'; filing deadlines table: non-listed companies 'Within seven months after FYE' (eight months with a share capital and an overseas branch register); listed companies within five months (six with a share capital and an overseas branch register)
citations.note: ACRA's filing-deadline guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the seven-month non-listed deadline and the table variants verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Due dates & requirements for AGMs
citations.locator: AGM due dates table: non-listed companies 'Within six months after FYE' (listed within four); exemptions: private companies that 'Send financial statements to all members within five months after the FYE' or qualifying dormant companies need not hold an AGM; private companies may dispense with AGMs by members' resolution; AGM details must be declared when filing the annual return; a member may request an AGM up to 14 days before the six-month deadline
citations.note: ACRA's AGM guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the six-month deadline, the five-month financial-statements exemption and the dispensation route verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Registering a local company via Bizfile
citations.locator: Registered office address requirements: 'Must be a Singapore address. Must be open and accessible to the public during normal business hours on each business day. Does not have to be the same place where you run your business activities'; the registered office is where ACRA and others send communications and notices and where company records and registers are kept; 'Must appoint at least one director that meets local residency rules during registration'
citations.note: ACRA's Bizfile registration guide fetched live 2026-10-23; the registered-office requirements and the local-director line verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Choosing company directors & other key officers
citations.locator: 'Every company must have at least one company director and one company secretary. A secretary must be appointed within six months of successful registration. The position cannot be empty for more than six months'; directors must 'Be ordinarily resident', be 18 or older, and 'Be a Singapore citizen, Singapore permanent resident, or someone who meets local residency rules'; the secretary must be a natural person meeting the local residency rules and 'Not be the same person as the sole director'
citations.note: ACRA's officers guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the six-month secretary deadline, the residency requirements and the sole-director bar verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Corporate Income Tax Rate, Rebates & Tax Exemption Schemes
citations.locator: 'Your company is taxed at a flat rate of 17% of its chargeable income. This applies to both local and foreign companies'; tax exemption scheme for new start-up companies (Income Tax Act 1947 s 43, revised from YA 2020): for the first 3 consecutive YAs, '75% exemption on the first $100,000 of normal chargeable income' and 'A further 50% exemption on the next $100,000 of normal chargeable income', a maximum exemption of $125,000 per YA
citations.note: IRAS's rate and exemption guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the 17% rate and the start-up exemption percentages verified on the page. Budget rebates (a 50% enhanced CIT rebate for YA 2026) change year to year; check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Do I need to register for GST
citations.locator: 'You must register for GST if your taxable turnover is: Under the retrospective view, more than $1 million at the end of the calendar year, or Under the prospective view, expected to be more than $1 million in the next 12 months'; worked retrospective example: turnover over $1 million for 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025 means applying 1 to 30 Jan 2026 with registration effective 1 Mar 2026; prospective view: 'you must apply for GST registration within 30 days after the date of your forecast', registered 2 months from the forecast date for liability arising on or after 1 Jul 2025
citations.note: IRAS's registration-liability guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the $1 million threshold, both views and the timing examples verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Who should receive CPF contributions
citations.locator: Under the CPF Act an employee is 'A person who is employed in Singapore under a contract of service'; 'You're required to pay CPF contributions for employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents earning total wages of more than $50 per month'; foreigners (persons who are not citizens or permanent residents) are exempted from receiving CPF contributions
citations.note: CPF Board guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the contract-of-service definition, the $50 floor and the foreigner exemption verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: How much CPF contributions to pay
citations.locator: Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 for monthly wages above $750: age 55 and below, 17% of wage by employer and 20% by employee (37% total), with lower bands above age 55; an increase to rates for senior employees takes effect 1 January 2027
citations.note: CPF Board rate tables fetched live 2026-10-23; the 17%/20% split for age 55 and below verified on the page. Rates change at budget events; check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance
citations.locator: 'the due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month'; 'Enforcement action will be taken against employers who fail to pay by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday)'
citations.note: CPF Board enforcement guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; both quoted deadline sentences verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Employment Act: who is covered
citations.locator: 'All employees under a contract of service with an employer are covered, but there are exceptions. For example, Part 4 of the Act which provides for rest days, hours of work and other conditions of service, does not cover managers or executives'; coverage spans local and foreign employees, full-time, part-time, temporary and contract, with seafarers, domestic workers and statutory board employees or civil servants excluded
citations.note: MOM's coverage guidance fetched live 2026-10-23; the quoted coverage sentence and the exclusion list verified on the page. Check the live page before relying.

citations.title: Employment Pass
citations.locator: 'The Employment Pass allows foreign professionals, managers, executives and technicians to work in Singapore. Candidates need to earn at least $5,600 a month. Employers must also demonstrate that they have fairly considered all jobseekers'; eligibility runs in two stages (the EP qualifying salary, then COMPASS), and jobs must be advertised on MyCareersFuture before applying
citations.note: MOM's Employment Pass overview fetched live 2026-10-23; the $5,600 qualifying-salary line and the two-stage eligibility structure verified on the page. The qualifying salary is higher for financial services and rises with age; check the live page before relying.
